entry.title: Attending events, 2023-2026
entry.summary: My game dev journey so far has been blessed with some opportunities to showcase my game and to network with fellow devs. Let's take a look back to what has has happened to Ardeimon these past few years.
entry.content:
My game dev journey so far has been blessed with some opportunities to showcase my game and to network with fellow devs. Let's take a look back to what has has happened to Ardeimon these past few years.

Electronic Sports and Gaming Summit (ESGS) 2022-2023

This was my first ever foray to public appearances related to game dev. This was also my first time ever attending a gaming-related event. I was really nervous showing my game to strangers and, honestly, a bit overwhelmed with the bug reports and feedback. Looking back, I've met some of my fondest acquaintances from these events.

On my 2nd ESGS attendance, I won the Globe Gen G award, the first time I've also accepted an award of that magnitude.

Philippine Game Dev Expo (PGDX) 2023-2026

PGDX came as a sort of an upgrade to ESGS as an entirely new event, with more booths, events and a highlight showcasing local indie games. Forgive the lack of variety in the pics. I'm really not much of a picture taker, and I didn't have a lot of time to take some. 

As I've gotten used to con-going (or more like con-showcasing), my experience of PGDX has been nice so far. It's a good place to connect with local players, meet some new friends and, you know me, learn through workshops. I would recommend applying for local devs!

Game Dev Summit (GDS) 2024, 2026

I was luckily invited to the first Game Dev Summit held at the Seawind Resort in Boracay last Feb 2024. This event is more catered to developers, for possible publishing and getting investments. There is a game showcase from various developers, networking events, talks as well as workshops.

Having a booth by the beach (yes, we were just meters away) was amazing. Despite being so near, I never really got to enjoy it. I was busy attending workshops. At least I'm a tiny bit wiser...?

I wasn't able to attend the 2nd GDS held at Boracay again last 2025, but made it to the 3rd one this time in Clark, Pampanga at Hilton Hotel. Instead of a separate booth, Craggenrock was included in the DTI Malikhaing Pinoy booth along with other finalists from the Young Creatives Challenge.

Like the first one, I really spent most of my time attending workshops and roaming around. 

Young Creatives Challenge, Season 1, 2024 (Defense and Finals)

I got into the finals of the first season of Young Creatives Challenge, game dev category last 2024. It's a nationwide contest across different creative categories. We scored 2nd place (or 1st runner-up, can't remember the exact title)!

LikhaSanay Game Dev Masterclasses, 2024

The game dev masterclass focused on game design. Iirc, there was a concurrent 3D-related class along with ours. We were comprised of a good and small selection of people involved in the game dev scene here in the Philippines, from indie devs to studio devs to the academe.

I don't have a lot of pictures of the actual classes because, if I remember correctly, we were not allowed to record or take pictures. There were some that were published publicly but I cannot find them anymore, unfortunately.

In retrospect

Game devs can have fun outside their games every once in a while. As someone who hasn't been part of the industry that long, I find it the whole experience welcoming and warm. I admit there have been multiple times I've felt I'm almost too isolated, but with the company of fellow devs and seeing interested players in these events, I'm reminded that is not the case. At this point, I'm not too sure if I'll be ever graced with similar opportunities in the future but I'm hoping to at least drop by and say hi to some of my newly-found friends from these events, even just through DMs.

If you're a budding game dev or if you just feel a little bit alone, try to bring yourself to events like this if you can. It might seem a bit daunting at first, but soon enough you'll feel like you rightfully belong.

We're done reminiscing. Consider stopping by my Bluesky and Instagram, and maybe you'll see something more in the present. Just maybe.

entry.title: Craggenrock tidbits
entry.summary: Here are some little things about Craggenrock some people might find interest in. Most of these are stuff I really could've posted as tiny tidbits for marketing, but well... 🤸.
entry.content:
Here are some little things about Craggenrock some people might find interest in. Most of these are stuff I really could've posted as tiny tidbits for marketing, but well... 🤸.

How did Craggenrock's development start?

Craggenrock started as an idea for an RPG similar to Summon Knight: Swordcraft Story around 2018. Early on, I already wanted to create something that heavily highlighted crafting. I planned it to be a bit more serious and stuff, but soon realized I was over-scoping my (first) game by a huge mile.

Multiple revisions years after, I "scaled" it down to focus on just the crafting because that's what I really wanted at the time. (I think I may have even stripped too much...)

If you want a more in-depth rationale behind Craggenrock and the crafting, I've already published a writeup on it years ago on Steam.

Where does the name "Craggenrock" come from?

It's really just crag and rock = Craggenrock. Everybody's so creative, amirite?

 

Everybody'S So Creative Tiktok GIFfrom Everybody'S So Creative GIFs

I love this woman. Hope she's okay.
Funnily enough, I was asked this very question during my presentation for the Young Creatives Challenge. You can already tell the judges were just as disappointed with my answer lol.

What was Craggenrock the game before it got its final title?

For the longest time, it was just Project Crafter to me. At some point, I wanted to reference the word "meteor" so it became Ameteos briefly. There was a Mallic phase too, related to malleus or hammer/mallet in Latin. Those names looked like they were trying too hard to be unique, so I dropped them.

How did you come up with the character names and locations?

Important characters are supposed to be allusions. Arlo, Luna and Hannah are exceptions.

  • Arlo - apparently means hill. Afaik, this was unintentional. It just seems like a name that's "soft" on the tongue and it sounded cute, so I went with it.
  • Luna - moon in Spanish. She has always been meant to be named like this. No special reason.

  • Braso - Spanish for arm. He's a reliable member of the town, a shoulder you can rely on.
  • Isalin - means to translate/transfer in Filipino. She moves around a lot, never in one place.
  • Karron - based on the Hiligaynon term for later, karon. Things you buy from him arrive later than immediately.
  • Pieza - Spanish for piece. She's named like this for a specific reason I cannot say because of possible spoilers.
  • Hannah - just a name I thought of, the particular reason of which I cannot share due to, again, possible spoilers. :)
  • Mano - Spanish for hand. It's more of a reference to the Filipino gesture of respect, pagmamano.

Adventurer names are just a collection of Spanish, Italian and Filipino names I could think of.

For the locations:

  • Town of Pareho - Filipino for same/similar. It's the town that will never be the same after the disaster. I think it's some sort of poetic self-contradiction in one way or another.
  • Halina Island - Filipino for "come along", an invitation. Similar to Pareho, it's meant to have that self-contradiction, seeing the island is infested with monster.

  • Tarong - Hiligaynon for proper. 
  • Sibucao - apparently a type of plant. There are some real places named like this.
  • Imbis - Filipino for instead.

  • Tikas Mining - Filipino for posture/poise. It's usually associated with muscular/fit builds, which are what I imagine healthy miners should be.
  • Three Cheers Tavern - This one has 2 intentions behind it.
    1. Three cheers usually refers to the "hip hip hooray" cheer. There's a popular segment in an old noon-time show that did this as a game. It's really frantic and fun.
    2. The three cheers are supposed to refer to the times adventurers/mercenaries will have a toast: one before heading out hoping things will go right, one during your escapade to drown out the stresses and one after you've come back, still alive. Some of them will probably only get to do the first 2. A bit somber, yeah. 😔

I use a lot of Spanish, Filipino and Hiligaynon references in the game due to my background. (I'm Filipino, Spanish is quite common in the Filipino language and I have lived in Iloilo for around a decade, making me familiar with Hiligaynon.) You'll see more examples in the following section.

How did you name the materials?

I wanted to break away from using the typical material progression (wood -> bronze -> silver, etc.), but also needed something that can hint what they're supposed to be, so I made all major materials follow a certain naming convention.

Ores

Ores are named after real life mountains/volcanoes + a suffix. The suffices indicate if they are a basic ore or an "alloy" as I would call them (ores that can result from combining other ores).

-on for the "alloys", -ite for the basic ones.

  • Marsilon - Marsili + -on
  • Tagron - Tagoro + -on
  • Malton - West Mata + -on

  • Saxanite - Saxani + -ite
  • Linzorite - Linzor + -ite
  • Elgonite - Elgon + -ite
  • Wistrite - Wister + ite
  • Galatite - Galatea + -ite

Craggenrock and Sunstone are unique, so both of them end with ground-related suffices (-rock and -stone). [Fun fact: Craggenrock the material used to be named Fragstone before!]

Wood
e.g. Navaro, Eder, Foster 

All wood are based on last names. I liked the idea of family trees. Arboris is different because it comes from arbor.

Yarn and Cloth
e.g. Madrigal, Falsetto, Medley

They are named after musical terms. I thought both music and cloth can flow.

Leather
e.g. Oroya, Sabal, Ensete

They used to be named after actual leather names, but I've since updated them. They're genus names for plants afaik.

Hides
e.g. Downy Hide, Porous Hide, Slippery Hide

I'll be honest, I kinda gave up on these lol. I just took whatever adjectives would work to describe rawhide.

Other Materials

I simply followed an adjective + noun pattern for most of them, being extremely careful not to use any terms that denote color or those that imply a certain level of quality. This is how we ended up with the likes of Cute Feather, Fragrant Herb and Thick Sap. Not very exciting, yes. A few of them are portmanteaus (e.g. Snaptalon and Gastracid).

Food

They're mangled references to real Filipino food.

  • Binitin - based on puto bumbong, but the name is derived from a different food called inipit.
  • Humuk - based on the plain puto. The name itself comes from the Hiligaynon word humok, which means fluffy/soft.
  • Karin-karin - based on carioca. The name is supposed to reminiscent of a different meal, kare-kare.
  • Gataan - based on ginataang bilo-bilo. I just took the gataan part.
  • Bucao - based on the Hiligaynon term bukaw, which afaik means big-eyed. There's an actual fish that fits this description called bukaw-bukaw in IIoilo, the red big-eyed fish.

  • Panabik - based on palabok. Panabik is a result of that mangling.
  • Rojas - based on the hotdog on a stick, the one with the marshmallow at the end. People usually associate that as a party staple in Filipino kids' birthday parties. Roja is just derived from rojo, Spanish of red. 'Coz we got red hotdogs here. (Yes, I know)
  • Binilog - based on the pianono bread. Binilog means "made round" in Filipino. Pianono afaik has that spiral pattern 'coz it's just sheet cake topped with cream, rolled then slice, explaining the spiral.
  • Bonanza - based on the banana que (or cue?). Bonanza is close enough to banana.
  • Subanon - based on chicken inasal. The Hiligaynon term for grilled food is sinugba. Subanon is derived from that.

  • Tanso - based on coffee. Tanso is the Filipino term for copper. Coffee is dark brown-ish, copper is brownish. You get the idea.
  • Lagundi - is actually just the name of the plant and the drink derived from it. It's known for cough relief. (Got a bit lazy with this one, tbh)
  • Darin - based on orange juice. I love citrus, especially mandarins 🤷
  • Maras - based on mango juice. There's a special variety of mangoes here that comes from the island of Guimaras.
  • Ginkurog - based on halo-halo. It's derived from ginakurog, Hiligaynon term for shivering.

These ones, I don't remember the name references to.

  • Sirado - based on kare-kare.
  • Sarian - based on the tinola.
  • Tatampo - based on the buko pandan.

That's it for now. I'll probably share more in another post.

If you're looking for something a bit more professional, try checking my posts on Bluesky and Instagram.
